description: Category glyph for a curated ingredient, which never carries a product photo. The vocabulary is closed — 21 values enumerated in pocket-nutrition-knowledge/schemas/ingredient.schema.json — and this maps 18 of them. sauce, seaweed and other are unmapped on purpose: no glyph reads unambiguously as any of them and a wrong icon is worse than none, so `expected` is null, never an empty string. Every mapped glyph is distinct, because two groups sharing one icon would defeat the point of a list meant to tell rows apart. Products and recipes are always food_group "other" server-side, so this never distinguishes a product from an ingredient — productType does.

cases.why: The largest group in the catalogue (381 ingredients), so the single most-rendered icon.
Second-largest mapped group (279). 🌾 is the grain rather than a bread loaf, which is baked_good — a port that conflates the two breaks here.
266 ingredients, and the pair-half of processed_meat below. Both must be present and distinct or cured and fresh meats render identically.
The other half of that pair. A port that maps both to 🥩 still passes the meat case.
243 ingredients behind a snake_case key. A port that camel-cases vocabulary keys breaks on this one, nut_seed and prepared_dish, and nowhere else.
🥛 was rejected because it is already the `glass` serving unit in serving-unit-emoji, and one glyph meaning two different things in the same UI is the collision this map avoids.
214 ingredients. Distinct from vegetable, which a single produce glyph would have merged.
195 ingredients. 🍯 is why `sauce` could not also be a jar — see the sauce case.
195 ingredients, and distinct from shellfish below.
Only 47 ingredients, so easy to drop while every fish case still passes.
138 ingredients. Snake_case key, and distinct from cereal.
134 ingredients. 🫘 is a recent codepoint — a port on an old font stack renders tofu, which is a rendering problem rather than a mapping one, and the string must still match.
134 ingredients, and the pair-half of alcohol. Merging them would put wine and orange juice under one glyph.
The other half of that pair, 100 ingredients.
125 ingredients — cooking oils, butters and lards. 🧈 rather than a bottle, which would have read as beverage.
95 ingredients behind another snake_case key.
🍲 was rejected because the suggestion list already uses it to mark a recipe row, and a prepared_dish ingredient wearing it would look like something that expands into a meal.
The smallest group (16 ingredients), so the one most likely to be missed.

The second-largest group in the whole catalogue (294) and still unmapped, which is the point: no glyph reads as "sauce" rather than as a jar, a bottle, or the 🍯 already taken by sweetener. 294 neutral placeholders beat 294 misleading ones.
In the vocabulary (29 ingredients), no glyph available. Distinguishes "no icon chosen" from "group not known", which a client must treat identically.

The catch-all, and the value the server assigns to every Open Food Facts product and every recipe. If this returned a glyph, every product without a photo would get it and the icon would stop meaning anything.
Knowledge can add a group to the schema before this map follows. The result is a missing icon, never a placeholder glyph and never an error.
The field is nullable on the wire. A port that indexes the map without a null guard throws here instead of rendering a row.
